reviewNotes:
• [Factual information] - Disembarkation timing: the notification gives disembarkation 4 min 8 s after the aircraft stopped (07:30:57, so about 07:35:05). The timeline entry gives 07:34:40 to 07:38:48 as a 4 min 08 s duration, starting when the airstair operated. The two cannot both describe the same interval.
  • Duty sign-on: the duty record gives 06:30 local, consistent with 11 h 00 min at 17:30. The pilot in command interview background gives 05:10 local.
  • Pilot in command's last simulator check: the duty record gives 11/03/2026. The interview background gives February 2026.
  • First officer's time with the company: the duty record gives 14 months. The interview background gives 17 months, but a joining date of April 2025 gives about 14 months at the occurrence.
  • Scaffold line for 07:30:02 ("five minutes after the end of civil twilight"): no last-light or twilight time appears in the evidence. It was not used.
  • Scaffold line for 07:30:33 ("No. 2 propeller was destroyed"): the inspection records three blades damaged beyond repairable limits. It was not used.
  • Timeline entry for 17/06/2026 21:35 cites the daily inspection log, but its supporting extract is the wildlife sighting log. No extract of the inspection log itself is attached.
  • Causal chain nodes (wildlife plan size threshold, fence repair deferred three budget cycles, Appendix 8A strike listing criterion, evening service schedule-change approval, rejected take-off training scope, runway edge lighting intensity) have no supporting documentary evidence in the material. These were marked not established in the factual section.
  • The result of the 24/06/2026 floor proximity lighting functional check is not recorded.
  • [Analysis / External Influences] - Timeline, "17/06/2026 21:35:00 Daily movement area inspection": the supporting extract attached is the wildlife sighting log, not the aerodrome daily inspection log cited as its source. The inspection log itself does not appear in the material.
  • Approved Factual information opening paragraph: "Sydney" as the destination and "50-seat" as the aircraft description do not appear anywhere in the material provided. They should be verified against source documents.
  • "Cabin floor proximity emergency lighting partially unserviceable" appears twice, under Safety issues and under Other risk factors, with identical tests, and is marked not finalised. Its intended category should be confirmed.
  • "Documented wildlife plan..." evidence says the aerodrome held no measures beyond the Aerodrome Manual 6.3 inspection. However, 10.4.3 requires the operator to be able to demonstrate what measures are in place, and a wildlife sighting log was maintained. Whether the log counts as a demonstrable measure is not addressed.
  • [Analysis / Organisational Influences] - Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles, Evidence and Significance: the separation between the fence pad and the carcasses is recorded three different ways. Evidence says the pad at 1,050 m was 110 m before the first carcass. Significance says the pad and carcasses were 140 m apart. The recorded positions (1,050 m, 1,188 m and 1,221 m) give 138 m and 171 m. The figure of 140 m also matches the length of the fence gap, so it may have been carried across by mistake. The draft gives positions only and does not state a separation.
  • Evening service approved as a schedule change, route risk assessment not reopened: the "Led to" edge points to "Runway inspection required only at listed aerodromes, and the listing criterion is a strike". That criterion is in Operations Manual Part A revision 9 (04/2024), which predates CMR-2025-118 (05/2025). The change could not have produced the criterion. It could only have missed an opportunity to catch its effect at Tarlton Springs, so the direction of the edge should be confirmed. The draft argues the missed opportunity only.
  • Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles, Existence note and Investigator notes: these describe the works register as "the operator's own register", but the source is the Tarlton Shire Council aerodrome works register. The draft uses "aerodrome operator" to avoid confusion with the aircraft operator. Confirm this is correct.
  • [Analysis / Risk Controls] - Training factor, Evidence: the crew's statement that every scenario they had been given was an engine event "arrived below V1" is contradicted by the TRG-SYL-07 extract. That extract includes an engine failure at V1 plus 5 kt, continued. The draft describes their statements only as engine events.
  • Runway inspection factor, Appendix 8A: the appendix states the list "is reviewed annually," but the last review is recorded as 03/03/2025. That is more than 15 months before the occurrence on 18/06/2026. This suggests the stated annual review was not met. Not included in the text; the investigator should confirm.
  • Timeline, 17/06/2026 21:35:00 daily movement area inspection: the entry cites "Aerodrome daily inspection log, 18/06/2026" as its source, but the attached extract is the wildlife sighting log (01/2025 to 06/2026).
  • Cabin floor proximity emergency lighting appears twice, under both "Safety issues" and "Other risk factors", with identical content. Its category label should be confirmed.
  • [Analysis / Local Conditions] - First officer sighting (timeline 07:30:31; lighting factor evidence against): the estimated range at first sight of around 200 m does not sit easily with the FDR distance reconstruction and runway survey. The aircraft was at 1,152 m at the reject, one second after the sighting call, and the carcasses were recovered at 1,188 m and 1,221 m. This suggests a range at first sight nearer 100 to 130 m, allowing for animal movement. The investigator may wish to reconcile or qualify the 200 m figure.
  • Timeline entry "Daily movement area inspection" (17/06/2026 21:35 UTC): the source cited is the Aerodrome daily inspection log, but the attached supporting extract is the wildlife sighting log description, not the inspection log.
  • Fifth sector factor: the "Evidence for influence" field contains importance-type content, while the "Evidence against influence" field contains both the argument for and the argument against. The field labels appear transposed or merged.
  • Runway edge lighting factor: the category is given as "Hypothesis (untested)", but the factor carries an Inconclusive Existence result and is listed under unresolved matters. The category label may need correcting.
  • [Analysis / Individual Actions] - Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay (Influence note): an estimated further 30 to 40 m from a stop 62 m into the RESA gives 92 to 102 m. That is beyond the end of the 90 m RESA, not "close to the far edge" as the note states. The draft gives the figures without the characterisation; the investigator should confirm which is intended.
  • Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay (Significance): this refers to an "asymmetric braking technique". No other evidence describes any braking technique beyond maximum braking with anti-skid on all four wheels and No. 1 reverse only. The draft omits the phrase.
  • Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay (Evidence): this says the No. 2 propeller was "destroyed". The inspection report records three blades damaged beyond repairable limits and one blade tip separation. The draft uses "damaged".
  • Timeline, 07:30:31 (first officer sights two kangaroos): the estimated range at first sight of around 200 m sits awkwardly with the other positions. Groundspeed reconstruction places the aircraft about 1,100 m along the runway at the sighting call, and the carcasses were found at 1,188 m and 1,221 m, roughly 90 to 130 m ahead. The figure may refer to a sighting earlier than the call; it was not used in the draft.
  • No runway inspection requested before the first departure after last light (Led to): this factor links to "Two kangaroos entered the runway strip and moved onto the sealed surface". An absent inspection would not cause the animals to enter; it would fail to detect or disperse them. The draft words the contribution as the animals being on the sealed surface during the roll. The investigator may wish to review the edge wording.
  • No runway inspection requested (Influence note): this refers to a "fence pad" in the 1,050 m to 1,250 m section. That item is not described in any of the evidence given in full here, so the draft mentions it only as recorded.
  • [Analysis / Occurrence Events] - "Two kangaroos entered the runway strip…" / engineering survey: the carcasses were recovered on the northern half of runway 09. However, the strike was taken by the right main gear and No. 2 propeller (the southern side on a 09 departure on the centreline), and the first officer said the animals had crossed the centreline moving south. The lateral positions do not obviously reconcile; the post-impact carriage of the carcasses may explain it but is not recorded.
  • "Two kangaroos entered the runway strip…": the first officer's estimated range of around 200 m at first sight does not fit the reconstruction. At 07:30:31 the aircraft was roughly 1,090–1,100 m along the runway (1,152 m at 07:30:32 at 115 kt groundspeed), and the carcasses were at 1,188 m and 1,221 m, which gives about 100–130 m. It may be worth stating that the 200 m figure is an estimate only.
  • "Deceleration achieved below…": the factor evidence gives the 2.6 m/s2 mean as "from maximum braking to the runway end", but the FDR readout gives it as the mean for 07:30:34 to 07:30:44. The runway end was reached at 07:30:51. The averaging interval should be confirmed.
  • "No. 2 propeller and right main gear struck two kangaroos", Significance: this says the strike removed a reverse unit "two seconds into a stop". The FDR places the impact one second after the reject (07:30:32 to 07:30:33). The draft uses the recorded timing.
  • "Deceleration achieved below…", Significance: the claim that neither the late start nor the reduced deceleration alone would have produced an overrun is not supported by any recorded counterfactual stopping-distance figures. The draft states it as the investigation's assessment; the supporting calculation may need to be added to the factual information.
  • [Conclusions] - Scaffold category "Contributing factors": this heading holds the cabin floor proximity lighting and the fifth-sector duty items, both of which failed Influence. The draft lists them under "Other factors that increased risk" instead, so that a heading does not describe them as contributing. The scaffold's "Probable cause" group of eleven contributing factors was split between the probable cause statement and the Contributing factors section.
  • Pad-to-carcass distance: "Perimeter fence repair deferred" gives the pad at 1,050 m as 110 m before the first carcass, and its significance field says the pad and carcasses are 140 m apart. "Two kangaroos entered" gives 138 m. The carcass is at 1,188 m, so 138 m is the arithmetic value.
  • Last light: the approved Factual information marks the time of last light or end of civil twilight as NOT ESTABLISHED. "Departure in the hour after last light" records the roll at 32 minutes after sunset and 5 minutes after the end of civil twilight (MET-ARCH-SB512-180626).
  • Fence, plan and procedure text: the approved Factual information also marks the fence condition and repair history, wildlife plan applicability, the Part A 8.14 and Appendix 8A text, the training syllabus and the evening service approval as NOT ESTABLISHED. All are documented elsewhere in the evidence and are relied on in these findings.
  • Duty start: "Fifth sector" gives sign-on at 06:30 local, but the Factual information notes the pilot in command's interview background gives 05:10 local.
  • Mislabelled field: in "Fifth sector", the field labelled "Evidence against influence" opens with "For influence:" and contains both arguments.
  • Causal chain timing: the chain "Evening service approved as a schedule change (CMR-2025-118, 22/05/2025) -> Runway inspection required only at listed aerodromes" runs backwards in time. Part A 8.14 revision 9 dates from 04/2024 and the list was last reviewed on 03/03/2025, both before the schedule change.
  • Inconclusive item on a causal chain: "Runway edge lighting intensity" (existence inconclusive) appears as a causal chain leading to "Take-off rejected 6 kt above V1", despite not being established.
  • Unsupported description: "Maximum braking and No. 1 reverse applied without delay" refers in its significance field to an "asymmetric braking technique", which no evidence item describes.
  • Excluded hypotheses: the scaffold lists them without terms. The draft uses their recorded existence term of "very unlikely".
  • [Recommendations / Documented wildlife plan required only above a size threshold the aerodrome does not meet] - Investigation log, 2026-07-02 entry: says two objects remain in draft "pending the fleet ballast answer and the glare question". The two unfinalised objects are the cabin floor proximity emergency lighting issue and the runway edge lighting intensity matter. The glare question plausibly relates to the edge lighting matter. No factor corresponds to a "fleet ballast" question, and the cabin lighting item was raised from the first officer's account rather than any ballast enquiry.
  • Cabin floor proximity emergency lighting partially unserviceable: this factor appears both under "Safety issues (organisational level)" and under "Other risk factors (safety issue)". Its category should be confirmed so it is not reported twice.
  • [Recommendations / Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles] - Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles, Evidence vs Significance: the Evidence places the animal pad at 1,050 m, "110 m before the point at which the first carcass was recovered", which puts the first carcass at about 1,160 m. The Significance places the carcasses at 1,188 m and 1,221 m, and says the pad and carcasses are "140 m apart". Pad to 1,188 m is 138 m and pad to 1,221 m is 171 m, so neither separation matches 110 m. The 140 m figure may have been conflated with the 140 m length of the fence failure. The distances were left out of the draft until they are reconciled.
  • Perimeter fence repair deferred for three budget cycles: the Importance test is recorded as Not tested. The subsection therefore rests the issue's significance on the recorded Influence and Significance entries, not on an Importance outcome.
  • [Recommendations / Evening service approved as a schedule change, route risk assessment not reopened] - Investigation log, 2026-06-19T01:20: records that the Head of Flying Operations suspended the evening Tarlton Springs service. The scaffold for this safety issue records no safety action. The investigator may wish to confirm whether the suspension should be recorded as safety action against this issue. If so, state whether it addresses the issue in full or in part: it removes the exposure but does not by itself correct the change management process.

It may come from the attached CMR-2025-118 extract, which is not reproduced here; the investigator may wish to confirm it against that document.
